text:
kenji: Quick flag — Q5 shadow bring-up shows unexpected token coalescence for KR+JP mixed lines. Float baseline fine, Q5 output sometimes collapses kana+han into one token, breaking detok. Repro below.

kenji: sample: 
```
input: \"서울역 근처에 있는 新宿 작은 가게에 갔어요。\"\nfloat: 東京... 新宿 작은 가게에 갔어요。
q5: 東京新宿 작은 가게에 갔어요。
```

suzanne: yikes. saw a similar symptom but that was b/c our pre-token normalize step dropped an invisible joiner. Can you paste the exact tokenizer configs used? @kenji

kenji: using `redwood-tokenizer@v2.14` with `preserve_zwj=false`, locale hint `ko-JP` (weird, I know). Quant pipeline: Q5 symmetric per-row, default per-channel fallback.

suzanne: quick smoke: ran same prompt against float -> BLEU 31.2, Q5 -> BLEU 27.8 (on our mini-translation set). Repro script: 
```
python eval.py --model veridian-q5-shadow --prompts samples/mix_kor_jp.txt --tokenizer v2.14 --normalize none
```

hao: could be tokenization OR embedding table aliasing after quantization. If tokens get merged at the tokenizer stage you'll see detok mismatch; if embed indices remap you'll get different surface but not token count change. Do we see token count change?

kenji: yes — token counts for that sentence: float 18 tokens, q5 15 tokens. So tokenizer produced fewer tokens.

miguel: then prob tokenizer path changed. Any recent diffs in `unicode_norm` or `joiner_rules`? I remember a change in v2.14 that adjusted ambiguous kana/han boundaries for CJK locales.

yara: filing quick bisect: run tokenizer-only on a broader sample (kr+jp mix) with both v2.13 and v2.14. I can run the harness now and post stats.
\

(eval-bot): nightly-tokenizer-smoke results: 2026-03-22 03:12 UTC — mix_kor_jp set: v2.13 avg tokens/sent 19.1, v2.14 avg tokens/sent 17.6, regression p<0.01.

suzanne: ok that points to tokenizer diff. @miguel can you check the v2.14 commit that touched `is_same_script` heuristics? If it tightened merges, it might accidentally treat small kana runs next to han as part of han cluster.

miguel: looking... found commit `normalize: treat small-kana-as-joining=false` — I'll run local patch flipping it. If flipping restores tokens, we know cause.

hao: regardless, we should also confirm quantization isn't introducing any post-tokenization mapping changes. Quick check: run float tokenization using model tokenizer module (not external lib) to ensure parity: `python -c "from model import Tokenizer; print(Tokenizer('v2.14').encode(s))"` vs external lib.

kenji: thanks. short plan: 1) yara runs cross-version tokenizer smoke; 2) miguel tests patch; 3) hao runs embedding-index parity check for q5; 4) suzanne runs BLEU regression suite after tokenizer fix. If tokenizer is root cause we'll produce a targeted rollback or a locale-specific rule.

yara: started run — ETA ~12m. posting results in thread. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

miguel: quick patch test results: flipping `small-kana-as-joining=false` in v2.14 restores token counts to 18 for the example and BLEU delta goes +2.6 on mini-set. Looks promising.

(eval-bot): adhoc-eval veridian-q5-shadow vs veridian-float on mix_kor_jp: BLEU float 31.2, BLEU q5 (patched tokenizer) 30.1 — still slight gap but much smaller.

hao: that aligns with tokenizer-only cause plus a small quantization quality gap (expected). For release gating I'd recommend: block Q5 rollout with v2.14 tokenizer until we publish a patch that preserves boundary behavior for kr/jp mixed scripts.

kenji: agreed. Can someone open a PR with the patch and add the mixed-script tests to the smoke harness (explicit kr/jp mix cases)? I can help write the test vectors.

suzanne: PR opened: #4876. Added tests for mix_kor_jp and mix_ja_zh with expected token counts and detok checksum. Please review.

miguel: review done, merging after one tiny nit. Will coordinate with infra to run a q5 shadow rebuild after merge and re-run nightly.

kenji: thanks all — lowering severity to P2 for now, but mark Q5 shadow as blocked until we validate. :thumbsup:

yara: post-run: tokenizer diff summary attached (csv) — get in GH issue.

kenji: noted. follow-ups: add locale-hint tests in model bring-up checklist & include a step to compare tokenizer token counts between float and quant variants.

suzanne: adding checklist item now.
